messages:
sam.reyes: FYI customer 'AcmeAI' on Private VPC reporting intermittent 403s from KMS during large embedding jobs + big latency spikes and a billing jump. Repro steps attached. @dmitri.kov can you take a look?

dmitri.kov: Thanks. Any example request IDs or timing windows?

sam.reyes: Seen across 2026-03-15 14:20-14:45 UTC window. Sample request id: req_8a3f4c. curl to our control-plane returns 200 but the agent logs show KMS 403s and HSM handshake errors.

maria.li: Uploading snippet from the control-plane logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:21:02Z INFO keyring: fetch attempt -> key_id=projects/acme/keyrings/r-123 version=1
2026-03-15T14:21:03Z ERROR kms: 403 Forbidden from kms.example -- reason=invalid-credentials
2026-03-15T14:21:04Z WARN hsm: handshake failed -> unexpected EOF, sessions=64/64
```

karina: Customer says traffic is all within their VPC -> private deployment, no public egress. They use a NAT gateway for KMS outbound.

tiago.ortega: Could be conntrack exhaustion on the NAT LB causing TCP resets and leading to incomplete TLS handshakes with the HSM/KMS. Any conntrack counters?

sam.reyes: Collected from the customer's edge NAT node:
```
# conntrack -S | grep entries
entries: 65535
# sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
65535
```

maria.li: That max is suspiciously low for high-throughput embedding batches. Also saw this in the agent: TLS handshake error + then immediate 403. HSM may be stateful and treats incomplete handshakes as auth failures.

dmitri.kov: Repro steps for us: 1) Run heavy embed worker with batch_size=512, concurrency=8 2) Observe NAT conntrack growth 3) See KMS 403 or HSM session limit in logs.

sam.reyes: Provided a minimal repro script from the customer:
```bash
#!/bin/bash
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -X POST https://private-agent.acme.internal/v1/embed -d '{"model":"embed-xxl","input":"$(head -c 2048 /dev/urandom | base64)"}' &
done
wait
```

karina: They also reported a billing spike at the same window — likely retries increasing token counts. Need to confirm if our client retries are exacerbating the conntrack problem.

tiago.ortega: Check iptables conntrack timeouts and ephemeral port exhaustion. Also confirm SNAT port limits on the NAT gateway (ports per IP ~ 65536). If each connection stays TIME_WAIT or tracked for long, you'll run out.

maria.li: I ran a quick audit on the customer's wire logs (pcap sample) — saw many SYN->RST and TLS ClientHello with no ServerHello. tcpdump snippet:
```
14:21:03.123456 IP 10.0.0.5.52344 > 35.196.12.8.443: Flags [S], seq 12345
14:21:03.123459 IP 35.196.12.8.443 > 10.0.0.5.52344: Flags [R], seq 0
14:21:03.124000 IP 10.0.0.5.52345 > 35.196.12.8.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:512 ack 1
```

dmitri.kov: Hypothesis: NAT conntrack full -> kernel starts dropping or resetting flows -> TLS handshake never completes -> KMS/HSM counts as auth failure -> 403. Also misbehavior if HSM side rate-limits by source IP and sees many half-open sessions.

sam.reyes: Customer wants guidance on immediate mitigations and a permanent fix. They're on our Private plan (VPC) so ops changes are customer-controlled but we should give a recommended runbook.

karina: Immediate steps: 1) Reduce embed worker concurrency and batch size (e.g., concurrency=2, batch=64) 2) Add exponential backoff on retries 3) Increase nf_conntrack_max to 262144 as emergency 4) Confirm NAT gateway SNAT port pool and increase if possible

tiago.ortega: Medium-term: enable connection pooling to KMS, reuse TLS sessions (session tickets) and use persistent sockets, or route KMS through a shared egress proxy with keepalive. Also tune conntrack timeouts: reduce tcp_fin_timeout and tcp_tw_reuse where safe.

maria.li: Added note: For HSM-backed KMS, check HSM session limits (customer reported 64/64 earlier). If HSM sessions are exhausted, KMS will deny new operations even with valid creds. Escalate to KMS provider if session limit is hit repeatedly.

dmitri.kov: I'll open an internal ticket to validate if our agent's KMS client is creating new TLS sessions per request. If so, we should patch to reuse connection pool for embedded workflows.

escalations-bot: Created escalation ticket E-2026-789 (owner: dmitri.kov) linking logs and customer repro. SLA: respond to customer within 2 business hours.

sam.reyes: Looping customer support: told customer to temporarily throttle and increase conntrack, they applied conntrack increase and saw immediate drop in 403s. Follow-up: they still see occasional spikes at peak.

karina: Next actions: 1) Dmitri to validate agent pooling patch + perf test 2) Tiago to draft NAT/conntrack runbook for Private VPC customers 3) Maria to confirm HSM session metrics and whether our KMS SDK surfaces those errors cleanly 4) Sam to keep customer updated

dmitri.kov: I'll run a controlled test tomorrow against a staging HSM with heavy parallelism and post results here.

sam.reyes: Thanks all, I'll update the customer that we're investigating and have a mitigation path. :thumbsup:
